book.title: The Group Chat Has Gone Quiet
book.author: Bea Lindqvist

lines: At 7:02 a.m. the group chat, which has a name I am not allowed to repeat, is silent.
This has not happened since 2019, when someone was foolish enough to ask whether pineapple belongs on pizza and four people had to be physically separated.
At 7:30 I send a photograph of my breakfast, which in this chat is a legally binding invitation to discourse.
By eight o'clock I have drafted three versions of a missing-persons announcement and eaten the bread I was saving for later.
At 8:20 a message appears from Chidi.
It simply says: "we're all in the other chat."
There has always been an other chat.
And somewhere in it, I now understand, a woman named Tola is describing my breakfast to everybody.
I type "who made the other chat" and hover over the send button, and feel, for the first time since primary school, entirely and magnificently unchosen.
